reforms.description: The R&D incentive for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) was extended for an additional two years, promoting innovation and investment in research activities. Additionally, a permanent 10% increase in the tax subsidy for R&D was estimated to raise the level of R&D spending by over 8%, alongside new measures including a temporary tax incentive for acquiring information infrastructure to support technological advancement.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The incentives are designed to increase R&D spending and promote innovation among SMEs, which supports economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The reforms have been actively implemented to support SMEs.
reforms.importance_rationale: The reforms significantly enhance existing R&D incentives but do not constitute a major overhaul of the system.
reforms.source_quote: A permanent 10% increase in the tax subsidy for R&D was estimated to raise the level of R&D spending by over 8%.

reforms.description: The MEXT launched a project to promote the diversification of the career path for researchers, enhancing their mobility within public research institutes.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Enhancing researcher mobility is expected to improve the overall quality and output of research, contributing to innovation.
reforms.status_evidence: The project has been launched and is currently in operation.
reforms.importance_rationale: The initiative is significant in promoting career diversification but does not represent a major structural change.
reforms.source_quote: The MEXT launched a project to promote the diversification of the career path for researchers in FY2006 and FY2007.

reforms.description: The 3rd Basic Plan of Science and Technology promotes cooperation between business and R&D organisations through conferences, facilitating knowledge transfer and collaboration.
reforms.package_name: Basic Plan of Science and Technology
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By fostering collaboration between businesses and research organizations, the plan aims to enhance innovation and commercialization of research outputs.
reforms.status_evidence: The plan has been actively implemented to promote cooperation.
reforms.importance_rationale: The plan is significant in promoting collaboration but does not represent a major overhaul of the existing framework.
reforms.source_quote: The 3rd Basic Plan of Science and Technology promotes co-operation between business and R&D organisations through conferences.

reforms.description: The amount of competitive grants for public R&D funds rose, increasing its share in central government outlays on science and technology.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Increasing competitive grants enhances funding availability for research, which can lead to greater innovation and productivity.
reforms.status_evidence: The increase in competitive grants has been implemented.
reforms.importance_rationale: The increase in grants is significant but does not represent a major reform of the funding system.
reforms.source_quote: The amount of competitive grants rose from 471 billion yen in FY2006 to 477 billion yen in FY2007.

reforms.description: The Japanese government has launched the 'New Industry Development Strategy 2005' to accelerate the development of the service sector, focusing on priority areas such as business services, software contents, health/welfare, and environment/energy. Additionally, the government has initiated the 'Program for Enhancing Growth Potential' to boost productivity growth across all industries, with a specific focus on raising productivity in the service sector.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: These initiatives aim to enhance productivity and innovation in the service sector, contributing positively to economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: Both initiatives have been actively implemented to support the service sector.
reforms.importance_rationale: The initiatives represent a major strategic shift towards enhancing the service sector's role in the economy.
reforms.source_quote: The 'Program for Enhancing Growth Potential' presented by the Council on Economic and Fiscal Policy (CEFP) in 2007 aims to boost productivity growth, as measured by value-added per worker, by 50% for all industries over five years.

reforms.description: The 'Special Zones for Structural Reform' initiative allows local areas to test regulatory reforms that can later be implemented nationwide, aiming to revitalize regional economies through deregulation.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: By allowing local experimentation with deregulation, the initiative aims to foster innovation and economic revitalization.
reforms.status_evidence: The initiative has been actively implemented to test regulatory reforms.
reforms.importance_rationale: The initiative represents a significant structural reform aimed at enhancing regional economic performance.
reforms.source_quote: The programme for 'Special Zones for Structural Reform' began in 2002; it marked the start of a fundamentally new approach in Japan, based on local initiatives to advance nationwide regulatory reform.
